records.title: Who commissioned the monitoring?
records.answer: ZHAW states that “Stadtgrün Basel” commissioned the five-year monitoring. The Basel government decision names Stadtgärtnerei as the public contact, so the exact contracting-unit name should be confirmed from the contract or protocol.
records.scope: Commissioning relationship; public-source wording only

records.title: When did the project start?
records.answer: The official ZHAW project page marks the project as ongoing and started in May 2026.
records.scope: Public project status as accessed 3 October 2026

records.title: What does ZHAW monitor?
records.answer: The public scope names four indicator areas: tree and understorey vitality, root development, infiltration capacity and soil-water balance.
records.scope: Named indicator areas; not a measurement protocol

records.title: What did Basel approve and why?
records.answer: In November 2025 the Regierungsrat approved CHF 280,000 for five years of scientific monitoring. The stated purpose is to assess the pilot elements for possible use elsewhere in Basel.
records.scope: Government expenditure decision and stated policy intent

records.title: Who leads the scientific work?
records.answer: Stefan Stevanovic is the project lead; Doris Tausendpfund is deputy. The published team also includes Axel Heinrich, Tal Hertig, Alain Bertschy and Nadin Iten.
records.scope: Team listed on the ZHAW project page

records.title: Is ZHAW the ground-truth partner?
records.answer: Yes—with a boundary. ZHAW is the primary empirical validation partner for the four published biophysical indicator areas at VoltaNord. That does not make it the ground-truth source for governance, social outcomes, maintenance cost, citywide transferability or impacts not named in the protocol.
records.scope: Role in this Decision Canvas, inferred from the commissioned monitoring scope

records.title: How should the Canvas connect to VoltaNord?
records.answer: The Canvas should screen upstream: identify a place, intervention mechanism and explicit expected effect. VoltaNord can then supply observed evidence for comparable implemented elements. The result should update the claim, its confidence and the screening rule—not be used as automatic proof for every site.
records.scope: Product architecture

records.title: What is not publicly shown as measured?
records.answer: The public VoltaNord description does not name air or surface cooling, sewer peak flow, combined-sewer overflow, flood damage, lifecycle cost, maintenance effort, public use, distributional equity or resident experience. These may not be claimed as monitored until the protocol confirms them.
records.scope: Absence from the public project description—not proof of absence from the internal protocol

records.title: Can VoltaNord prove an effect elsewhere in Basel?
records.answer: Not by itself. VoltaNord can validate observed performance under its own design, soils, weather, construction and maintenance conditions. Transfer to another site requires a comparability check and may require new measurement or modelling.
records.scope: Scientific use of site-specific monitoring

records.title: How long does the monitoring run?
records.answer: The project description and Basel decision say five years from a May 2026 start. A ZHAW research-group listing displays May 2026 to August 2034. The discrepancy is unresolved and should be confirmed with the project team.
records.scope: Public date metadata

records.title: Where is the monitoring protocol?
records.answer: No public protocol was found in the checked official pages. We still need definitions, instruments, sampling sites, baselines, comparison design, cadence, quality controls, data ownership, publication schedule and reuse terms.
records.scope: Targeted public-source check completed 3 October 2026

records.title: Which future decision will each result change?
records.answer: The public rationale is possible citywide application, but no decision rule is published. The group should ask which thresholds, standards, design details or investment choices will be updated—and who signs off on that update.
records.scope: Learning-to-decision hand-off

records.title: Has ZHAW made similar monitoring understandable before?
records.answer: In the separate Grüze Living Lab project, ZHAW describes sensor and plant-assessment data being visualised interactively and in near real time. This is a useful access precedent, but it does not prove that VoltaNord uses the same method or publication model.
records.scope: Separate project; method and communication precedent only

records.title: Request a 60-minute evidence hand-off with ZHAW and Stadtgärtnerei
records.answer: Ask for the protocol, indicator definitions, site and comparator design, measurement cadence, first reporting milestone, data fields, licences, confidentiality limits and named contact for future updates. Resolve the 2031/2034 date discrepancy in the same meeting. Also ask for the 2024 three-street measurement concept (project 74640) and whether it is the basis of the VoltaNord protocol.
records.scope: Immediate research action

records.title: Use a four-step claim ladder
records.answer: Store claims separately as: mechanism supported by external evidence; effect expected at a screened site; effect observed at VoltaNord; effect judged transferable to a new site. Never collapse those four states into one “potential effect” badge.
records.scope: Evidence model for the Decision Canvas

records.title: Create a VoltaNord learning agreement
records.answer: Agree who can see raw and processed data, when results are released, how caveats travel with every chart, which city standards may change, and who records the decision. Publish at least a compact indicator dictionary and reporting calendar for the wider group.
records.scope: Governance of evidence and group access

records.title: Is VoltaNord a public or private development case?
records.answer: The wider area has several owners, including Basel-Stadt, SBB and Stiftung Habitat. The public monitoring pages do not identify the ownership and operating responsibility of every monitored street element. The atlas should therefore classify each element—not the whole area—before assigning a public, private or mixed decision route.
records.scope: Ownership of individual monitored elements

records.title: Why split new development, retrofit and renewal?
records.answer: They are different decisions. New development can reserve space and performance before design is fixed. A retrofit must justify changing an asset that is still operating. A scheduled renewal can attach sponge-city requirements to work that will happen anyway and avoid replacing the old condition like for like.
records.scope: Decision-atlas organising model

records.title: Is any VoltaNord code, sensor schema or data public?
records.answer: No. A search of GitHub (ZHAW orgs, opendatabs, keyword code search), Zenodo, ZHAW digitalcollection, ORCID and data.bs.ch found no code, sensor schema, processing pipeline, protocol or dataset for VoltaNord or for ZHAW project 74640. Details and the list of searches are in docs/ZHAW-SOURCES.md.
records.scope: Public-source search completed 3 October 2026; sources not listed there remain unchecked

records.title: Did ZHAW already design a Basel measurement concept?
records.answer: Yes. The 2024 project Schwammstadt-Vegetationsbausteine für Basel-Stadt (client: Stadtgärtnerei) states that a measurement concept was designed to document effectiveness at three street locations. The concept, the street names and any results are not public.
records.scope: Project-page statement only; content unknown

records.title: Which three Basel streets does the 2024 measurement concept cover?
records.answer: Unknown. It is also unknown whether they are in VoltaNord, and whether the 2024 concept became the 80788 protocol. Ask for this explicitly; it is the most useful unpublished artefact.
records.scope: Open until ZHAW or Stadtgärtnerei confirms
records.question: Which three streets, and is the 2024 concept the basis of the VoltaNord protocol?

records.title: Which instruments does the ZHAW team use elsewhere?
records.answer: In the Zurich Scheuchzerstrasse project (81151, same team, started July 2026) ZHAW names visual vitality scoring (Bonituren), dendrometer measurements and soil sensors for tree growth and the substrate's water and energy balance. The sensor type is not stated.
records.scope: Zurich project; not confirmed for VoltaNord

records.title: Will VoltaNord use the same instruments?
records.answer: Probably similar: same team, same indicator families and a parallel start. Treat vitality scoring, dendrometers and soil-water sensors as the working assumption for the Place Profile fields, but mark them inferred until the protocol is shared.
records.scope: Working assumption for schema design only

records.title: What has the team published about tree substrates?
records.answer: Two EFUF 2023 slide decks on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0): a Wädenswil field trial of structurally stable substrates for green infrastructure and stormwater management, and Zurich sponge-city substrate and vegetation systems. They are slides only, with no data, and count as mechanism-supported evidence, not observed Basel effects.
records.scope: Mechanism evidence; claim-ladder level 1

records.title: Which ZHAW student or conference work is reusable?
records.answer: Kommunizierende Baumrigolen (connected tree trenches, CC BY 4.0) gives a requirement checklist for the tree-trench intervention. Beläge in der Schwammstadt (2026 talk; licence not specified) covers infiltration of permeable paving. The Gundeldinger Feld thesis (CC BY 4.0) measured cooling under irrigated green roofs in Basel.
records.scope: Context and mechanism evidence; not VoltaNord

records.title: Which Basel open data can fill the Place Profile now?
records.answer: data.bs.ch offers CC BY 4.0 datasets for tree inventory and felling list, canopy cover, land cover, groundwater level, water-protection zones and the meteoblue climate network. They cover need and possibility screening. None measures soil water, infiltration or VoltaNord performance.
records.scope: Catalogue check 3 October 2026

records.title: How did Berlin structure street-tree soil-water data?
records.answer: QTrees stores readings as tree_id + sensor type + timestamp + value. The four types are suction tension at 30, 60 and 90 cm, plus a stem-area/average channel. Watermark sensors by ARBOR revital sit in the tree pit at the three depths. Raw sensor readings live in a private schema; nowcasts and 14-day forecasts per tree are public. Model features are month, genus, tree age, shading index, wind, temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, watering events and yesterday's mean value. The model is a random forest. Code is MIT-licensed.
records.scope: Read from the public repositories; Berlin irrigation context

records.title: How did Berlin make suction tension understandable?
records.answer: Baumblick maps suction tension to three classes: Gut (0–33], Mäßig (33–81], Kritisch (81–270]. The code does not state the unit. Watermark sensors normally report centibar (= kPa), so kPa is the likely unit, but that is inferred.
records.scope: Thresholds verified in code; unit inferred

records.title: Can QTrees results stand in for VoltaNord?
records.answer: No. QTrees forecasts irrigation need for existing Berlin street trees in conventional tree pits. It does not measure infiltration, stormwater retention or sponge-city substrates, and its thresholds are not calibrated for Basel soils or ZHAW substrates. Use it as a schema, modelling and communication precedent only.
records.scope: Transfer boundary

records.title: Is QTrees still running?
records.answer: No. The project ran September 2021 – September 2023 with EUR 410,544 of BMUV funding (German climate adaptation programme DAS). It deployed more than 120 sensors in Mitte and Neukölln and got no follow-up funding. Baumblick runs in demo mode with static data (since July 2024); the backend's last commit was June 2024.
records.scope: Status at 3 October 2026

records.title: How should the Place Profile hold soil-water evidence?
records.answer: Follow the QTrees long format: site/tree id, variable (e.g. suction tension at a named depth), timestamp, value, unit and origin (observed or modelled). Keep the raw value and any display class separate. Leave the class thresholds unset until VoltaNord or Basel calibration exists.
records.scope: Schema proposal for the Decision Canvas; not yet implemented

records.title: Where is VoltaNord on the map?
records.answer: The map draws the official development-plan perimeters BP 226A (Areal VoltaNord) and BP 226B (VoltaNord 2. Stufe), both in force since 16 June 2026. This is the planning perimeter. It is not the set of streets or elements that ZHAW monitors; those sites are not public.
records.scope: Planning geometry from the zoning overlay dataset; monitoring sites unknown

decision_routes.question: How should a new public development build sponge-city performance in from the start?
decision_routes.accountable_role: Public project owner, with the competent planning, water, mobility and green-space offices
decision_routes.caution: A design label such as “sponge city” is not a performance requirement. Specify measurable functions and who will maintain them.

decision_routes.question: How can a new private development be governed or incentivised?
primary_levers: building-permit requirements within the legal basis
land-sale or lease conditions where the public owns land
decision_route: review evidence at planning and permit gates
decision_routes.accountable_role: Competent planning or permit authority; landowner where contractual conditions apply
decision_routes.caution: Do not treat an incentive as a requirement or imply powers the authority does not have. Record the exact legal, contractual or voluntary basis.

decision_routes.question: How should a multi-owner new development make one water and green-space system?
decision_route: bind agreements before permits or disposal
decision_routes.accountable_role: Area-development lead with every affected owner and infrastructure operator
decision_routes.caution: A technically connected system can fail institutionally if ownership, access, liability and maintenance stop at parcel lines.

decision_routes.question: What can be changed in public infrastructure before a full renewal is due?
primary_levers: temporary test followed by capital decision
decision_route: identify urgent need or low-regret opportunity
choose reversible pilot or permanent retrofit
decision_routes.accountable_role: Operating asset owner, with BVD-led cross-office coordination where functions conflict
decision_routes.caution: Retrofitting outside the renewal cycle costs more and disrupts operations; use it where urgency or learning value justifies that premium.

decision_routes.question: How can existing private land contribute when no major project is planned?
primary_levers: utility or runoff incentive where legally available
decision_routes.accountable_role: Programme owner in government or a delegated delivery partner; the property owner remains asset steward
decision_routes.caution: Voluntary programmes can select for willing owners rather than highest-need places. Track who participates and who is left out.

decision_routes.question: How can a retrofit work when runoff, roots or access cross ownership boundaries?
decision_routes.accountable_role: Named convenor with authority to keep all owners and operators at the table
decision_routes.caution: Do not begin with construction if the party responsible for overflow, root damage or maintenance is unresolved.

decision_routes.question: What should happen when a public street, sewer, square or building is already being renewed?
decision_route: flag climate opportunity before scope freeze
include option in credit and design
decision_routes.accountable_role: Renewal project owner; portfolio board owns the cross-asset opportunity check
decision_routes.caution: The crucial data is often the decision window. A perfect map that arrives after scope and budget are fixed cannot influence the project.

decision_routes.question: How should sponge-city measures enter a private renovation?
decision_routes.accountable_role: Competent permit or incentive programme owner; private owner remains delivery and maintenance owner
decision_routes.caution: A renovation does not automatically authorise every desired condition. Separate mandatory, negotiated and incentivised measures.

decision_routes.question: How can public and private renovation cycles be synchronised?
decision_route: deliver and evaluate as one system
decision_routes.accountable_role: A named programme or area coordinator; each owner retains statutory and asset decisions
decision_routes.caution: The opportunity disappears if either side learns about the other project after procurement or permit approval.
